name: Kiss It Goodbye
label: Revelation
lede: Tim Singer and Keith Huckins left Deadguy, took the rhythm section of Rorschach, and moved to Seattle to make one album. They split before the Sub Pop EP they'd recorded could come out.

eras.title: Out of Deadguy and across the country
eras.text: Singer and Huckins walked out of Deadguy and pulled in the bass and drums of Rorschach. They practiced in New York until the songs were tight, then relocated to Seattle.

years.src: No Echo: Interview · Hex Records · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
years.h: Tim Singer and Keith Huckins walk out of Deadguy
years.p: Huckins blames band politics. Singer wanted Seattle, Huckins didn't care where they lived, so they called Thom Rusnak and Andrew Gormley of Rorschach and went.
years.xp:
The plan, as Singer tells it to Hex Records, was to get Rorschach back together with him singing. Before leaving the East Coast they "practiced like crazy," cut a demo called Be Afraid that got passed around New York, and played a run of New York shows. The demo is the only recording with guitarist Eric Cooper.

Singer says they all moved to Seattle within a few months. He'd first hoped to keep Deadguy going as a touring band: "I sort of wanted to have my cake and eat it too."

years.src: No Echo: Interview · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
years.h: Billy Anderson records the album at Ironwood in Seattle
years.p: Why Anderson? Huckins answered in one word: Neurosis, the band Anderson had recorded.

eras.title: Nine songs, a tour, and a floor to sleep on
eras.text: She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not came out on Revelation and made the metal press. Then the band toured with Unsane and Obituary, and the road wore out the guitarist who'd started it.

years.src: Wikipedia: She Loves Me · Revelation Records · No Echo: Tim Singer
years.h: She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not is Revelation REV 58
years.p: Nine songs in 45 minutes, from Fire Drill at under two to Sick Day at eight and a half. Terrorizer ranked it No. 17 of 1997; it hit No. 13 on CMJ's Metal Top 25 that July.
years.xp:
The first vinyl run was 1,220 black and 317 clear.

Singer built his vocals from a phrase or two at practice rather than writing lyrics out in advance, and near the end of the band's run he dropped the lyric sheet and improvised on stage. No Echo counts [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]], [[Daughters|c9368a03-bf26-40b6-bdfa-9af8d10b568b]] and [[Young Widows|c9e69e05-2c05-4700-a311-53fe4ffc649e]] among the bands it rubbed off on.
play: She Loves Me, She Loves Me Not

years.src: Revelation Records · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
years.h: Two songs the LP left off go out on a 100-copy red 7"
years.p: Preacher and Target Practice come out on Revelation. A second pressing of 330 follows on gold.

years.cap: Flyer for Kiss It Goodbye at CBGB, Sunday, May 18, 1997
years.src: Flickr (Change Zine) · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
yt: Kiss It Goodbye at CBGB, May 18, 1997
years.h: Out on the road with Unsane and Obituary
years.p: Kiss It Goodbye spend 1997 touring with New York's [[Unsane|db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b]] and Florida's [[Obituary|2e8ac3ed-2a89-4377-ba80-790106aba554]]. A CBGB matinee on May 18 put them on a bill with Coalesce, the Rye Coalition, Black Army Jacket and Mason.
years.xp: The flyer billed the CBGB date as the last New York-area show of the tour. A fan filmed the set, and a full set from Houston's Fitzgerald's survives too.

years.big: "I didn't want to drive 12 hours to a 15 person show"
years.src: No Echo: Interview · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
years.h: Huckins quits; Seattle's Demian Johnston takes his guitar
years.p: After the 1997 tours, guitarist Keith Huckins leaves Kiss It Goodbye, and Demian Johnston steps in.
years.xp:
Huckins told No Echo the rest of the picture: staying on a floor at the end of the drive. The novelty had worn off.

Johnston went on to [[Playing Enemy|61b0f945-ce01-4925-950e-fbc5ce389957]].

eras.title: Three songs for Sub Pop, a farewell on Revelation
eras.text: Kiss It Goodbye recorded three songs for a Sub Pop EP, and then Singer quit. The tapes sat until Revelation put them out.

years.src: Hex Records · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
years.h: Singer quits with three songs in the can for Sub Pop
years.p: He's around 30, with marriage and young kids ahead, and has decided hardcore isn't something you do into your thirties. The band ends with him.

years.h: The Sub Pop songs finally appear, on Revelation, as Choke
years.p: A 7" and a five-song CD, produced by Matt Bayles and Billy Anderson, come out a year after the sessions.
years.xp: The CD adds earlier unreleased material from around the album sessions. The 7" ran 220 on purple vinyl, then 330 on orange.

eras.title: Two returns, one for a friend
eras.text: Kiss It Goodbye came back twice: a short West Coast run in 2012, and in 2025 the original album line-up played Brooklyn to raise money for the family of New York hardcore promoter Rich Hall.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye · Revelation Records
years.h: Singer and Rusnak take a new line-up down the West Coast
years.p: Guitarist Alex Miller and drummer Neal Witmer fill out the band. Revelation re-presses the album on white vinyl, 560 copies, for the tour.

years.h: Singer's Bitter Branches release Your Neighbors Are Failures
years.p: His newer band, with [[Dan Yemin|bfac6050-54c5-4b29-bb73-465c90e6e327]] on bass, puts the full-length out on Equal Vision.

years.src: Brooklyn Vegan · Wikipedia: Kiss It Goodbye
years.h: The album line-up plays Warsaw for Rich Hall's family
years.p: Singer, Huckins, Rusnak and Gormley reunite in Brooklyn. Hall, the 1000 Knives and CBGB promoter, died in January 2025.
years.xp: The Warsaw bill also had [[From Autumn to Ashes|a6bfadac-d028-4bda-a5b2-e1468f556569]], [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]], Harvest and [[Skycamefalling|a8aa0797-dab7-4bcd-a2ef-e5e0fff5f309]]. The next night at Brooklyn Monarch, [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], [[Cave In|f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05]] and [[Deadguy|311e7afe-e0e3-476a-a703-fcd61dc049ac]] played the second Rich Hall show.
